summary: Partial only. The all-orders flag-transitive-plane conjecture is unresolved. Complete Python replay excludes counterexample orders n<251539607552 under the imported premises. Two arithmetic implementations report matching decision digests through n<2582236504064, conditional on their correct executions; that entire interval is not Python-replayed. The inherited endpoint 10341223092224 still rests on one entire-range run. Novelty is unknown.

claims.statement: The seven published isolated base-two controls have residue 1. D is verified planar for n=2,8, while n=24,90,512 have explicit difference collisions; n=134217728 has a proper factor of p, and n=297474474 fails valid necessary congruences. These isolated checks are not a reproduction of the full published interval.

Assume p=n^2+n+1 is prime, n>8, D=mu_(n+1) is planar, and the valid divisor-multiplier condition. Then gcd(n,3*5*7*17*31)=1. More generally the multiplicative subgroup generated by divisors of n cannot contain a second ordered pair of difference 1 in addition to (2,1). This elementary necessary-condition corollary is not asserted to be new and does not resolve the conjecture. Likely prior art includes Hall (1947), Cyclic projective planes, and successors; no priority conclusion is made.

For every integer exponent a with 3<a<59049, p=2^(2a)+2^a+1 is composite except a=9, where D=mu_513 in F_262657 is not planar by an explicit collision. Thus, under the declared geometric reduction, no non-Desarguesian flag-transitive plane has power-of-two order 2^a in that exponent range. This covers only that family, not arbitrary orders; a>=59049 is not excluded by this claim. Novelty is unknown. These witnesses probably reproduce known Cunningham-type factorizations.
claims.check_command: python3 -c 'import json; d=json.load(open("evidence/power-two-family.json")); assert [r["a"] for r in d["factors"]]==[3**t for t in range(3,d["first_unresolved_t"])]; assert all(1<r["proper_factor"]<(1<<(2*r["a"])) and ((1<<(2*r["a"]))+(1<<r["a"])+1)%r["proper_factor"]==0 for r in d["factors"]); print("PASS: full-integer proper factors for entire chain")'

claims.statement: For every fixed finite sieve bound B, all sufficiently large t give n=2^(3^t)>8 with n=8 mod 24 such that p=n^2+n+1 has no prime factor <=B, while every positive divisor d of n satisfies d^(n+1)=1 mod p (including d=2). Thus a fixed finite-factor sieve plus these necessary power conditions has infinitely many integer survivors. This asserts neither that any such p is prime nor that D is planar or any counterexample plane exists. It is a limitation of the filtering strategy, not a solution or refutation of the contract.

The two retained C backends match all 960 exact full-residue vectors, including 90 synthetic positive vectors at 65-94-bit odd moduli. Python manual exponentiation rechecks every stored residue. These are finite arithmetic controls, not natural plane-shaped survivors or a general-range proof.

Every one of 9999 even orders in [2,20000) has its actual sieve factor and complete ordinary power residue rechecked by Python trial division and exact powers. A separate Cipolla-root replay matches both C decision digests. A divisor q is accepted only when 1<q<p; prime controls are not sieved by themselves. This is a small-order control only.

Two new unsieved C runs report exactly 2,8,24,90,512,134217728,297474474 among all 2499999999 even orders in [2,5000000000). Their full-residue block digests agree for every order, and their binary hashes are in their headers. Python rechecks 1384 recorded full residues only. This control covers the unsieved small-modulus path (p<2^65), not the main sieve or full main-range arithmetic; entire control executions are not replayed in Python.

Two preserved C executions with different modular multiplication (three radix-2^32 limbs versus two radix-2^64 limbs) and different root algorithms report zero unsieved base-two survivors for n=8 mod 24 in [200000000000,2000000000000). Their decision hashes agree in every one of 8941 consecutive common blocks, covering 75000000000 members. EVERY decision hashes the actual factor or the complete ordinary residue of an unsieved power; factor records explicitly have an uncomputed residue. Assuming the imported premises AND correctness of these executions, these orders are excluded. Python-only replay fully checks only the separately claimed prefix blocks and recorded samples; it does not certify this entire production interval. Both programs share author, compiler, OS, exponentiation recurrence, and hashing implementation. Conditional on the imported premises AND on that single entire-range execution being correct, it gives n<10341223092224. Reconstructed logs match the staged recovery manifest; hashes establish integrity, and sieved+tested counts are bookkeeping. New paired runs and Python replay corroborate only their explicitly stated subsets. No binary hash in the old log header links that run to a retained executable.

For even n>2 and prime p=n^2+n+1, D=mu_(n+1) is planar if and only if sum_j (-1)^j binom(t(n+1),j(n+1)) is 0 mod p for every even t in [2,n-2]. This follows by finite-field power sums and an invertible Vandermonde matrix. It supplies no all-orders inconsistency proof, is not used to skip scan members, and is likely a classical cyclotomic criterion; novelty is unknown.
